summary: B2 Mirror Chat V2 missing-target validation — 3/4 backend integration tests PASS, 1 CRITICAL integration bug found. Health OK. Live POST /api/mirror/chat is unaffected (200 on all three scenarios, no new B2 fields leaked into the response body). Receipt collection writes correctly when an explicit about_person_id is supplied (target_resolution_status=RESOLVED) and correctly does NOT false-fire on a no-proper-name message. HOWEVER the headline B2 guarantee — that a chat message containing a NEW proper name produces a receipt with target_unresolved_name and proposed_action.type='add_to_circle' — FAILS end-to-end for Pete (and by extension any user whose saved_people live in db.saved_people rather than db.people).
rca_of_issue:
Two compounding root causes prevent the missing-target fallback from ever running through the live shadow pipeline:

1) /app/backend/routers/mirror_chat.py:144 — `_b1_load_saved_people` queries `db["people"]` (legacy collection). The canonical saved-people store is `db.saved_people` (used by services/saved_people.py, services/member_chart_resolver.py, services/relationship_resolver.py, services/mirror_chat_pipeline.py, services/home_insight_v6.py). Pete has 9 docs in db.saved_people and 0 in db.people, so saved_people=[] reaches the shadow glue.

2) /app/backend/services/mirror_chat_shadow.py:73 — `if about_person_id or saved_people:` gates the call to `resolve_relationship_context`. When both are falsy the router is NEVER invoked, so the new missing-target fallback (relationship_router_v2.py lines 235-266) has no opportunity to fire. The persisted receipt has `relationship_resolution: null` and `target_resolution_status: 'NOT_APPLICABLE'` even when the message contains a clearly-unresolved proper name.

Reproduction: POST /api/mirror/chat with {user_id: '697f0c6abf35c0528ff06954', message: 'How does Sarah show up at work?'} → 200 OK, but the receipt for that request has target_unresolved_name=null, proposed_action=null, target_resolution_status='NOT_APPLICABLE'. The relationship_router_v2 unit tests still pass (7/7) because they call resolve_relationship_context directly; only the integration path is broken.

Mitigation (for main agent):
  a) In services/mirror_chat_shadow.py drop the `if about_person_id or saved_people:` gate — always call resolve_relationship_context so the proper-name fallback can fire even with empty saved_people. (Or, equivalently, also call it when message contains capitalised tokens.)
  b) In routers/mirror_chat.py change `_b1_load_saved_people` to read from `db.saved_people` (collection used everywhere else). Map the docs to the {id, name, role, closeness, weight} shape that relationship_router_v2 expects.
  c) After (a) and (b), re-run /app/backend/tests/test_b2_mirror_chat_shadow.py — test_mirror_chat_unresolved_named_sarah should pass.

critical.issue: B2 missing-target fallback never fires end-to-end. routers/mirror_chat.py:144 reads legacy db['people'] (empty for canonical users), and services/mirror_chat_shadow.py:73 only calls resolve_relationship_context when about_person_id or saved_people is truthy. Net effect: receipts for messages mentioning a new proper name have relationship_resolution=null and target_resolution_status='NOT_APPLICABLE'. The promised target_unresolved_name / proposed_action telemetry is silent.

minor.issue: Live response is unchanged ✓ but on the explicit-target path the receipt records missing_data=['target_not_in_saved_people'] AND target_resolution_status='RESOLVED' simultaneously — slightly contradictory telemetry when about_person_id refers to a person the shadow loader can't see. Will resolve naturally once the saved_people collection bug above is fixed.

verified_guarantees.live_response_unchanged: PASS — response body across all three scenarios contains only response/session_id/timestamp (+ optional debug/evidence/thread/memory_update). No target_unresolved_name, proposed_action, or target_resolution_status leakage.
verified_guarantees.resolved_path_correct: PASS — about_person_id='6a0b0ac57a933e4a69a5183b' yields receipt with target_resolution_status='RESOLVED' and proposed_action=null.
verified_guarantees.no_propername_no_falsefire: PASS — 'Tell me about my chart' yields receipt with target_unresolved_name=null and proposed_action=null.
verified_guarantees.unresolved_named_path: FAIL — 'How does Sarah show up at work?' should yield target_unresolved_name='Sarah' + proposed_action.type='add_to_circle'. Instead receipt has relationship_resolution=null and target_resolution_status='NOT_APPLICABLE'. See rca_of_issue.

action_items: FIX services/mirror_chat_shadow.py:73 — remove the `if about_person_id or saved_people:` gate or expand it so resolve_relationship_context is invoked whenever a chat request arrives (the router itself is fast and side-effect-free). This is the single change that unblocks the headline B2 telemetry guarantee.

FIX routers/mirror_chat.py:144 — replace `db['people'].find_one({'user_id': request.user_id})` with a read from `db.saved_people.find({'user_id': request.user_id}).to_list()` and map docs to the {id, name, role, closeness, weight} shape consumed by relationship_router_v2. The legacy `people` collection is empty for current canonical users.

Verify the relationship_resolver._derive_frame logic also covers the lens=None / life_domain=None case correctly once saved_people are loaded (currently returns 'self' which is fine, but worth confirming the fallback triggers for that frame as the router code already allows).
critical_code_review_comments: services/mirror_chat_shadow.py — `_derive_frame` contains `return 'forum' if False else 'self'` which is dead code (always returns 'self'). Should be cleaned up or replaced with the intended branch.

routers/mirror_chat.py is enormous (>1500 lines for a single endpoint) and the shadow hook is nested inside the main try/except. The shadow logic should be its own small helper so the saved-people loading is visible/auditable from one place — would have caught the db['people'] vs db.saved_people drift at review time.

build_receipt computes target_resolution_status off of `rel.get('target')` truthiness, but when relationship_resolution is null the status is 'NOT_APPLICABLE' regardless of whether the message had a proper name. Consider letting the validator do its own proper-name detection as a defence-in-depth so the receipt telemetry survives a future shadow-glue regression.

The INTENT_ROUTER_V2_SHADOW gate defaults to true (intent_router_v2.shadow_mode_enabled). Confirmed shadow receipts are being persisted on every chat call — good. Cutover flag INTENT_ROUTER_V2_CUTOVER is correctly still false.
